# Global Business News Today

> Business news and analysis on global markets, central banks, SMEs and startups, technology and AI, and commercial real estate.

Global Business News Today is an independent business news website. Articles cite primary sources such as SEC filings, central bank statements, government statistics and company announcements, and link to them inline. Every article page includes NewsArticle structured data with its publication and update dates.

- Editorial contact: info@globalbusinessnewstoday.com
- Sitemap: https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/sitemap.xml
- RSS feed: https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/feed.xml

## Site Sections

- [Home](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/): Latest global business news and top stories
- [All News](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/all/): Every article, newest first
- [World Business](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/world/): Global economy, trade, energy and industrial policy news for business leaders.
- [Markets & Finance](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/markets/): Central bank decisions, interest rates, inflation and financial market analysis.
- [Tech & AI](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/tech/): Enterprise AI adoption, cybersecurity and business technology news.
- [SMEs & Startups](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/smes/): Small business finance, cash flow, venture capital and startup funding news.
- [Real Estate](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/property/): Office markets, commercial property, conversions and real estate finance.
- [Press Releases](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/category/press-releases/): Corporate announcements and press releases distributed by Global Business News Today.

- [Anthropic IPO Filing: Revenue Hits $33.2 Billion in Nine Months as Net Loss Reaches $104 Billion](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/articles/anthropic-ipo-filing-q3-2026-results/): Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows Q3 revenue of $17 billion and a $104 billion nine-month net loss, mostly a non-cash charge tied to its rising valuation. - [Fed Holds at 3.75% to 4%, Signals More Hikes: What Higher Rates Mean for SMEs](https://globalbusinessnewstoday.com/articles/fed-rate-cuts-global-markets-2026/): The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, and the ECB and BoE lean hawkish as energy lifts inflation.
